DH&M: Copper Pots and Pans Tinned in Rhode Island

Oh man, talk about fancy. I picked up a 8.25" pan for my dad and a small fry pan for myself on their other site, eastcoasttinning.com. I've never cooked with copper before, probably because it was so freaking expensive, but I figured hey, let's see what the fuss is about. I checked the directions and they were very specific to make sure something was in the pan before you turned the heat on, and make sure the heat never goes past medium. Strange. I thought to make scrambled eggs my first time around. I threw a pad of butter in the pan and lit her up. Instantly, and I mean within 3 seconds, the butter was melted. Shit, hadn't even gotten the eggs scrambled! I cracked the eggs into the pan and turned the heat to low (I was at medium high before). The flame was small but the entire pan became consistently hot. It was something I'd never seen before. I was used to being able to boil a pot of water, look down at the bottom of the pan and bubbles coming from a rough outline of the flame. Not here. It was ALL hot. The eggs cooked in a minute and a half and that was the end of it. I placed the pan off to the side and let it cool. Not going to lie, I'm still worried I'll melt the tin inside (which the directions state is a very real possibility if you don't pay attention to what you're doing), but for now I'm in love with copper pans!
